_comment.7: DO NOT CLOSE THIS LOOP ON THE NUMBERS AS SHIPPED. BOTH the delay AND the

params._roi_note: start_x/start_y centre the 32x32 ROI on the beam parked at coarse bias 2/2 (fine 1.5/2.15): probe-verified 2026-07-21, full-sensor CoM (x 919, y 507). Re-derive with contrib/probe_frame.json only if the alignment (not the bias) changes -- the ROI now follows the beam by cropping instead of re-biasing.

pipeline._comment: full-rate [y,x] ERROR record (BEFORE fsp, so it is the measured error, not the command). Distinct filename from steering_fsp.json so a parport run does not overwrite a piplate run.

pipeline._delay_warning: THE ONE THING THAT DOES NOT CARRY OVER. delay/delay_frac below (global/x 5+0.8, y override 5+0.6) were fit with the BRIDGEplate in the loop. The parport DAC removes ~0.5-1.4 ms of transport, which at fs 3788 (264 us/frame) is roughly 2-5 frames -- a large fraction of the 5.8 fr configured here. The values are left UNCHANGED on purpose rather than guessed at: an over-modeled delay degrades rejection, but UNDER-modeling is the known failure mode (the 2026-07-16 run under-modeled by 1.6-2.3 fr and spiraled at ~310 Hz once the ramp passed ~50% authority), so erring long is the less dangerous direction to sit in while unmeasured. Re-fit from conf_bode_par_x/y.json (full-band 5-300 Hz phase slope) and update BOTH the global and the y override before this file is trusted.
pipeline._note1: THE CONTROLLER. Delay is measured from the BODE PHASE, not the departure latency. broad_order=512 and broad_mu=.03 match attenuation11.
pipeline._K_warning: THE K VALUES BELOW ARE PLACEHOLDERS, NOT MEASUREMENTS. Ky=0.66 / Kx=0.915 are the piplate-era numbers and do NOT apply to this setup, for two independent reasons: (a) the fine channel is DIVIDED downstream, so a DAC volt no longer reaches the FSM as the volt it used to, and (b) scale here is 1.0 V/unit against the old 2.0, halving the volts per command unit on its own. Both push the true K DOWN, so the configured values are too LARGE -- which is the safe direction: u = -phi_hat/K, so an over-large K under-drives the command. Under-driving degrades rejection; UNDER-estimating K over-drives and is how you get runaway. Replace both from the <=30 Hz plateaus of conf_bode_par_x/y.json before quoting any result from this file.
pipeline._note2: K is the SIGNED command->error gain (error units per command unit). Its SIGN (y +, x -) is a property of the optical/mechanical path and does carry over; only the magnitude is invalid. K is also bias-dependent and shifts with every re-centre.
pipeline._note3: With broad_order>0 the identified full-band observer supplies the command and the AR2 modal estimate is not added, avoiding double cancellation. The modal q/r values remain available for diagnostics and for rollback with broad_order=0.
pipeline._note4: zeta ~0.002 = sharp line; ~0.3 = broadband hump. adapt_period>0 turns on Petit/Meimon re-identification every 8 s. Set adapt_period 0 for a fixed FSP while first validating on the new transport.

params._fs: 3788 inherited from the piplate era. The camera should still be the bottleneck, but the DAC no longer adds to the loop period -- confirm the achieved rate and update fs (and bode_plot's sample_rate) if it has moved, since delay in FRAMES depends on it.
params._broad_lp: 2026-07-22 observer band-limit: 11-tap boxcar prefilter on the NLMS input kills the 300-420 Hz command-echo regeneration (the 380 Hz x limit cycle) at the root; +5 frames folded into the broad horizon, in-band timing unchanged. Note the regeneration frequency fs/(2*(delay+delay_frac)) MOVES when the delay is re-fit for this transport -- if the new delay is much shorter, re-check that broad_lp's first null still sits usefully relative to the new band.
params._guard: burst guard: per-axis band-pass detector on the raw error at the regeneration freq fs/(2*(delay+delay_frac)). CURRENTLY OFF (guard_ratio 0), inherited from steering_fsp.json where the 316/344 Hz detector false-tripped on low-frequency leakage. Re-evaluate on this transport: with a shorter delay the regeneration band moves UP, which may put it clear of the leakage that caused the false trips.

y._K: PLACEHOLDER 0.66 (piplate-era). Replace from conf_bode_par_y.json's <=30 Hz plateau -- see _K_warning above. Expect well below 0.66.
y._delay: 5+0.6 = 5.6 fr, PIPLATE-ERA. See _delay_warning above -- re-fit from fsm_bodey_par.pdf.

x._K: PLACEHOLDER 0.915 (piplate-era). Replace from conf_bode_par_x.json's <=30 Hz plateau -- see _K_warning above. Expect well below 0.915.
x._delay: x inherits the global 5+0.8 = 5.8 fr, PIPLATE-ERA. See _delay_warning above -- re-fit from fsm_bodex_par.pdf.

pipeline._note: PARPORT DAC. TWO channels only -- there is no coarse stage: ch0 = y/tip (DACA, +1.0 V/unit) = index 0, ch1 = x/tilt (DACB, -1.0 V/unit) = index 1. The fsp output is plain [y,x] in command units.
pipeline._range: 0-5 (unipolar, DACRANGE code 0x0), biased at mid-range 2.5 V so the command has 2.5 V of headroom in BOTH directions without needing a bipolar range. 76 uV/LSB -- 2x finer than +-5, since all 16 bits cover 5 V instead of 10. Same range, offset and scale as conf_bode_par_x/y.json, which is REQUIRED: K is measured in error-units per command-unit, so a bode taken at a different scale would not transfer.
pipeline._avss_note: GROUND AVSS for this unipolar range (EVM J17 pin 5) -- do not run it at -12 V. SLASEH2A 7.5 specifies the unipolar accuracy figures AT AVSS = 0 V (TUE +-0.07 %FSR, offset error, zero-code error 0.15 %FSR); the -21.5 V <= AVSS < 0 conditions are the BIPOLAR ones. Unipolar on a negative AVSS is inside Recommended Operating Conditions (7.3: AVDD 4.5..41.5 V, AVSS -21.5..0 V, AVDD-AVSS 4.5..43 V) but is not a characterized combination, and it doubles analog dissipation (~192 mW vs ~96 mW at AIDD/AISS 8 mA typ). AVDD needs VMAX+1.5 = 6.5 V, so +12 V is ample.
pipeline._footroom_note: This loop commands down to 1.5 V, which is NOT threatened by the 1.25-1.5 V headroom/footroom figure: SLASEH2A 7.5 conditions that on -10 mA <= load <= 10 mA (1.25 V) or +-15 mA (1.5 V), and even then it is a distance from the RAIL, i.e. from 0 V once AVSS is grounded. At 1.5 V with a light load there is no issue. If the FSM driver does pull ~10 mA, meter the actual output at the bottom of the command range before trusting it, and only then consider a negative AVSS -- which trades the characterized unipolar condition for footroom.
pipeline._authority_check: clamp is +/-1.0 and scale is 1.0 V/unit about a 2.5 V bias, so the loop commands 1.5..3.5 V -- 10x the +/-100 mV the bode probes with, and comfortably inside 0-5 either way. That number was CHOSEN, not measured: it follows from making command units = volts so the bode amplitude reads directly in mV. If the FSM needs more, raise `scale` (and re-run the bodes at the new scale, since K scales with it) or widen `clamp`. If it is more authority than the mechanism should ever get, lower `clamp` -- the safer knob, and it does not invalidate K.
pipeline._range_max: AUTO-RANGING. range_max 0-10 lets the device widen a channel's output range when the commanded voltage no longer fits 0-5, and narrow it again once the command has sat inside 80% of the narrower range for shrink_dwell iterations (default 4000, ~1 s at 3.8 kHz). It steps through the LADDER, picking the narrowest range that fits: 0-5 -> 0-6 -> 0-10, so 0-10 is a ceiling, not a jump. All three are legal on the +12 V rail (unipolar needs AVDD >= VMAX+1.5), though 0-10 leaves only 0.5 V of margin -- drop range_max to 0-6 for a comfortable 4.5 V if you never expect to need the full swing.
pipeline._range_max_polarity: The ladder stays UNIPOLAR: range_contains() excludes +-5 and the other bipolar ranges here, because 0-10 does not contain -5..+5. That is correct for a 2.5 V-biased command that never needs to go below ground. If you ever DO need negative output, set range_max to a bipolar range instead (e.g. "+-5", which does contain 0-5) -- the ladder then becomes 0-5 -> +-5 and can reach below 0 V.
pipeline._range_max_glitch: A range change still shows ONE intermediate value -- DACRANGE is a resistor gain network (SLASEH2A 8.3.2) and re-interprets the code already in the active register the instant it lands, so for one frame (~6.4 us) the output is neither the old voltage nor the new one. It cannot be made zero (two ranges express the same voltage for one code only where they intersect, i.e. 0 V), but the device picks the write order that minimises it: writing the new code BEFORE DACRANGE makes the output move TOWARD zero and then land exactly on target, instead of the old order's overshoot AWAY from it. 0-5 -> 0-10 at 4.9 V shows 2.45 V rather than 9.8 V. An undershoot toward ground is a far safer transient for a mirror than a 2x overshoot in the direction it was already moving. Holding LDAC does NOT avoid this: SLASEH2A 8.3.3 gates only the DAC DATA registers (buffer -> active), while DACRANGE changes the gain applied to whatever the active register holds. That is also why sync_update forces the old, larger order -- it is off here.
pipeline._range_max_dormant: NOTE AS CONFIGURED: clamp +/-1.0 at scale 1.0 about the 2.5 V bias bounds the request to 1.5..3.5 V, which already fits 0-5 -- so auto-ranging can NEVER trigger here and is purely a safety net for if you later widen scale or clamp. parport_dac logs a warning at startup saying exactly this. If you want it live, the clamp is what has to move.
pipeline._scale_sign: y positive, x negative -- the same signs the piplate config used (+2/-2), only halved in magnitude. The sign is a property of the optical/mechanical path, not the converter. A wrong sign is POSITIVE feedback: verify with a push test before closing, and fix it here rather than by flipping the sign of K.
pipeline._sync_update: left OFF. With two driven channels the async skew is one frame, ~6.4 us -- about 2% of the 264 us loop period, and below the platform's own ~6.8 us SCHED_FIFO / ~32 us C-state jitter. sync_update would remove that skew at the cost of a third frame per iteration. Turn it on only if axis cross-coupling shows up that tracks scheduling hiccups rather than the command; see doc/devices/parport_dac.md, Update mode.

params._verify: off in the closed loop: verify turns each write into 3 frames (write, read-command, NOP) plus a non-posted status read per bit. Use conf_parport_dac_smoke.json to exercise it before a run, not the loop itself.
params._skip_unchanged: kept, but expect it to skip far LESS than on the BRIDGEplate: at 153 uV/LSB the command changes the code far more often than 1 mV codes did. That is fine -- a frame is ~6.4 us against a ~264 us period -- but it does mean the DAC sees more traffic than the piplate config did.
